claim: Gastruloids are 3D aggregates of mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: Here, using gastruloids –3D aggregates of mouse embryonic stem cells- we study the formation of one of the three germ layers, the endoderm.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a definition of gastruloids.

claim: The endoderm is generated from an epiblast-like homogeneous state by a three-step mechanism in gastruloids.
source: We show that the endoderm is generated from an epiblast-like homogeneous state by a three-step mechanism: (i) a loss of E-cadherin mediated contacts in parts of the aggregate leading to the appearance of islands of E-cadherin expressing cells surrounded by cells devoid of E-cadherin, (ii) a separation of these two populations with islands of E-cadherin expressing cells flowing toward the aggregate tip, and (iii) their differentiation into an endoderm population.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the three-step mechanism observed in the study.

claim: Islands of E-cadherin expressing cells are surrounded by cells expressing T-Brachyury during the flow.
source: During the flow, the islands of E-cadherin expressing cells are surrounded by cells expressing T-Brachyury, reminiscent of the process occurring at the primitive streak.
evidence: This observation is directly stated in the abstract.

claim: Endoderm formation in gastruloids does not require an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition.
source: Consistent with recent in vivo observations, the endoderm formation in the gastruloids does not require an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, but rather a maintenance of an epithelial state for a subset of cells coupled with fragmentation of E-cadherin contacts in the vicinity, and a sorting process.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding and references consistency with in vivo observations.

claim: Gastrulation is a crucial stage of animal development that results in the laying down of the body plan through the specification of the germ layers.
source: Gastrulation is a crucial stage of animal development that results in the laying down of the body plan through the specification of the germ layers – the endoderm, the mesoderm, and the ectoderm – and their organization with reference to three orthogonal axes (Wolpert et al., 2006; Solnica-Krezel and Sepich, 2012; Williams and Solnica-Krezel, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Defects in gastrulation result in premature death or birth defects.
source: Defects in gastrulation result in premature death or birth defects (Ferrer-Vaquer and Hadjantonakis, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Mammalian embryos develop in the uterus of the mother, which makes gastrulation difficult to study.
source: Mammalian embryos are different, in that an increase in the cellular mass is concomitant with gastrulation (Snow, 1977; the fact that they develop in the uterus of the mother makes this coupling and the process of gastrulation difficult to study).
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the introduction.

claim: Upon exposure to external cues and morphogens, gastruloids show an intrinsic capability to polarize, elongate and pattern in a manner that is reminiscent of the early embryo.
source: Upon exposure to external cues and morphogens, gastruloids show an intrinsic capability to polarize, elongate and pattern in a manner that is reminiscent of the early embryo (van den Brink et al., 2014; Turner et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: 3D gastruloids exhibit a multiaxial organization and spatiotemporal patterning of Hox genes.
source: Strikingly, 3D gastruloids exhibit a multiaxial organization and spatiotemporal patterning of Hox genes (Beccari et al., 2018) with signatures of somitogenesis (van den Brink et al., 2020; Veenvliet et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Aggregates exposed to Chiron lose their spherical morphology and acquire a teardrop shape.
source: Aggregates exposed to Chi lose their spherical morphology and acquire a teardrop shape (Figure 1B, day 4, Video 1).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by figure and video references.

claim: Approximately 80% of aggregates exposed to Chiron qualify as elongated.
source: We find that 30/37 or ~80% aggregates qualify as elongated with an elongation threshold set to 0.125 (see also Video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study.

claim: 75% of control aggregates remained spherical.
source: In contrast, 15/20 or 75% of control aggregates remained spherical (Figure 1b, day 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing control aggregates.

claim: An E-cadherin-rich region is observed at the pointed end of Chiron-exposed aggregates.
source: At the pointed end of the Chi exposed aggregates, we observed an E-cadherin (E-cad)-rich region, which was absent in the control aggregates (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: The E-cadherin pole emerges from an initially homogeneous distribution of E-cadherin.
source: The E-cad pole emerges from an initially homogeneous distribution of E-cad (Figure 1D, Video 3).
evidence: This temporal observation is stated and supported by figure and video references.

claim: A T-Brachyury-rich pole emerges from a spatially homogeneous distribution at day 3.
source: Likewise, a T-Brachyury (T-Bra)-rich pole, clearly visible at the tip of the aggregate at day 4, emerges from a spatially homogeneous distribution at day 3.
evidence: This temporal observation is explicitly stated.

claim: E-cadherin is expressed from the early time points.
source: While E-cad is expressed from the early time points (Figure 1D, day 2), T-Bra expression follows exposure to Chi (Figure 1D and Video 4).
evidence: This temporal expression pattern is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: T-Brachyury expression follows exposure to Chiron.
source: While E-cad is expressed from the early time points (Figure 1D, day 2), T-Bra expression follows exposure to Chi (Figure 1D and Video 4).
evidence: This temporal relationship is explicitly stated.

claim: The Chiron pulse triggers a decay in E-cadherin level.
source: The Chi pulse triggers a decay in E-cad level (mean intensity, Figure 1E and Video 5).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure and video references.

claim: T-Brachyury level is maximal just before removal of Chiron and gradually decreases thereafter.
source: T-Bra level, maximal just before removal of Chi, gradually decreases thereafter (Videos 2 and 6).
evidence: This temporal pattern is stated and supported by video references.

claim: Most aggregates show a single pole of T-Brachyury (35/64).
source: Most aggregates show a single pole of T-Bra (35/64), some display multiple poles (18/64) and 11/64 do not polarize (Video 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the study.

claim: E-cadherin and T-Brachyury polarize prior to the onset of tip formation.
source: Using descriptors of aggregate's shape and polarization of fluorescence signal (see Materials and methods), we found that E-cad and T-Bra polarize prior to the onset of tip formation (Figure 1F and G), suggesting a possible role of E-cad and T-Bra in the aggregate's shape polarization.
evidence: This temporal relationship is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: E-cadherin and T-Brachyury may play a role in the aggregate's shape polarization.
source: Using descriptors of aggregate's shape and polarization of fluorescence signal (see Materials and methods), we found that E-cad and T-Bra polarize prior to the onset of tip formation (Figure 1F and G), suggesting a possible role of E-cad and T-Bra in the aggregate's shape polarization.
evidence: This is presented as a suggestion based on the temporal relationship observed.

claim: A group of E-cadherin expressing cells is localized at the tip, spatially segregated from and surrounded by T-Brachyury expressing cells.
source: As shown in Figure 2A, a group of E-cad expressing cells is localized at the tip, spatially segregated from, and surrounded by T-Bra expressing cells.
evidence: This spatial organization is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The core of E-cadherin expressing cells expresses Sox17.
source: Furthermore, we observed that this core expresses Sox17 (Figure 2A, inset, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and Foxa2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 7) – markers of the endoderm.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: The core of E-cadherin expressing cells expresses Foxa2.
source: Furthermore, we observed that this core expresses Sox17 (Figure 2A, inset, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and Foxa2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 7) – markers of the endoderm.
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: Sox17 and Foxa2 are markers of the endoderm.
source: Furthermore, we observed that this core expresses Sox17 (Figure 2A, inset, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) and Foxa2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Video 7) – markers of the endoderm.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Sox2 is present earlier but absent at 5 days post-plating while Sox17 is retained.
source: We confirmed that Sox2 is present earlier but absent at 5 days-pp while Sox17 is retained (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This temporal expression pattern is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The group of E-cadherin expressing cells demarcates an endoderm-like region in the gastruloids.
source: These observations lead us to conclude that the group of E-cad expressing cells demarcates an endoderm-like region in the gastruloids.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the marker expression data.

claim: The core of E-cadherin/Sox17 expressing cells and the T-Brachyury expressing cells constitute the majority of the cell population near the tip.
source: The core of E-cad/Sox17 expressing cells and the T-Bra expressing cells constitute the majority of the cell population near the tip (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: A minority of cells outside the core express either Sox17 alone or in conjunction with T-Brachyury.
source: Nevertheless, a minority outside the core expresses either Sox17 alone or in conjunction with T-Bra.
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated.

claim: The E-cadherin/Sox17 expressing cells form a tightly packed group of cells.
source: The E-cad/Sox17 expressing cells that form the core maintain a relatively larger simply-connected-component (126 of 131 Ecad+/Sox17+ cells) and a homotypic neighborhood (111 E-cad+/Sox17+ cells maintain an Ecad+/Sox17+majority neighborhood), which implies that they form a tightly packed group of cells.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the connectivity analysis.

claim: The T-Brachyury expressing cells form multiple simply connected-components suggesting they are sparsely distributed around the core.
source: In contrast, the T-Bra expressing cells form multiple simply connected-components (20 components) suggesting that they are sparsely distributed around the core.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the connectivity analysis.

claim: At early stages, E-cadherin expression pervades the entire aggregate and is present at every cell-cell contact forming a homogeneous network of junctions.
source: At the early stages E-cad expression pervades the entire aggregate; It is present at every cell-cell contact forming a quite homogeneous network of junctions.
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated.

claim: The E-cadherin junctional network undergoes a gradual fragmentation.
source: However, this network undergoes a gradual fragmentation (Figure 3A and Videos 8–11).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure and video references.

claim: The level of E-cadherin decreases temporally while a small fraction is retained, which eventually localizes near the aggregate's tip.
source: The level of E-cad decreases temporally while a small fraction is retained, which eventually localizes near the aggregate's tip.
evidence: This temporal pattern is explicitly stated.

claim: Some E-cadherin/T-Brachyury cells express lower levels of E-cadherin compared to their neighbors devoid of T-Brachyury.
source: Within our immunostainings, we found consistently the presence of some E-cad/T-Bra cells that express lower levels of E-cad compared to their neighbors devoid of T-Bra (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, 92 hrs-pp).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: A gradual repression of E-cadherin via increasing levels of T-Brachyury may account for the fall of the E-cadherin level in the junctional network.
source: In view of earlier studies (Turner et al., 2014; Fernando et al., 2010), a gradual repression of E-cad via increasing levels of T-Bra may possibly account for the fall of the E-cad level in the junctional network.
evidence: This is presented as a possible explanation based on earlier studies.

claim: At 72 hours post-plating, only a small fraction of cells distributed in a salt and pepper manner express Foxa2.
source: Furthermore, in immunostainings at 3 days-pp, we notice only a small fraction of cells – distributed in a salt and pepper manner – that express Foxa2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At 72 hours post-plating, there is no organized group of cells that can potentially yield the endoderm.
source: Therefore, at 72 hr-pp, we do not find an organized group of cells that can potentially yield the endoderm.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the observations.

claim: At 72 hours post-plating, the cell population can be broadly classified into three categories: cells expressing both E-cadherin and T-Brachyury, cells expressing only T-Brachyury, and cells expressing only E-cadherin.
source: Additionally, at this stage, the cell population in the aggregates can be broadly classified into three categories: a class of cells that express both E-cad and T-Bra and two classes that express either one of the two markers (Figure 3B, left).
evidence: This classification is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The E-cadherin+/T-Brachyury- cells are the ones expressing Sox2, akin to an epiblast.
source: Additionally, the E-cad+/T-Bra- cells are also found to be the ones expressing Sox2, akin to an epiblast.
evidence: This observation is stated with an interpretation.

claim: The E-cadherin/T-Brachyury expressing cells constitute most of the cell population (~70% of the total).
source: The E-cad/T-Bra expressing cells constitute most of the cell population (~70% of the total) and are surrounded by the T-Bra expressing cells (Figure 3B, right).
evidence: This quantitative observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: At later time-points before aggregates are fully polarized, an 'archipelago' of E-cadherin expressing cells separated by T-Brachyury expressing cells is observed.
source: Interestingly, at later time-points but before the aggregates are fully polarized, we observed an 'archipelago' of E-cad expressing cells separated by T-Bra expressing cells (Figure 3D, 92 hrs-pp, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: At day 4, the E-cadherin expressing cells exhibit low levels of N-cadherin and Snail1.
source: At day 4, the E-cad expressing cells exhibit low levels of N-cadherin and Snail1, supporting the absence of an EMT transition for the E-cad expressing cells (Figure 3—figure supplements 1C and 2).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: Low levels of N-cadherin and Snail1 in E-cadherin expressing cells support the absence of an EMT transition.
source: At day 4, the E-cad expressing cells exhibit low levels of N-cadherin and Snail1, supporting the absence of an EMT transition for the E-cad expressing cells (Figure 3—figure supplements 1C and 2).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the marker expression data.

claim: The data are consistent with recent observations in the mouse showing endodermal progenitors do not undergo EMT.
source: These data are consistent with recent observations in the mouse (Scheibner et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with published work.

claim: The islands of E-cadherin expressing cells are positive for the pluripotency marker Oct4.
source: Additionally, the islands of E-cad expressing cells were found to be positive for the pluripotency markers Oct4 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Oct4 expression correlates inversely with T-Brachyury expression.
source: The Oct4 expression correlates inversely with the T-Bra expression, suggesting pluripotency and an epiblast-like nature of these cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This correlation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The inverse correlation between Oct4 and T-Brachyury suggests pluripotency and an epiblast-like nature of E-cadherin expressing cells.
source: The Oct4 expression correlates inversely with the T-Bra expression, suggesting pluripotency and an epiblast-like nature of these cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the correlation data.

claim: The endoderm-like region originates from islands of pluripotent and epithelial cells expressing E-cadherin.
source: Altogether our data suggests that the endoderm-like region - identified at the end of day 4 – originates from islands of pluripotent and epithelial cells expressing E-cadherin.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: There is a directed flow of cells towards the future region that will form the tip of the gastruloid.
source: The flow field clearly shows that there is a directed flow of cells towards the future region that will form the tip of the gastruloid (Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, and Videos 15–17).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure and video references.

claim: E-cadherin-negative cells flow backward at the periphery, away from the tip.
source: E-cad- cells flow backward at the periphery, away from the tip, which creates a physical separation between the two populations: E-cad+ and E-cad- cells (Videos 8–10).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by video references.

claim: The backward flow of E-cadherin-negative cells creates a physical separation between E-cadherin-positive and E-cadherin-negative cell populations.
source: E-cad- cells flow backward at the periphery, away from the tip, which creates a physical separation between the two populations: E-cad+ and E-cad- cells (Videos 8–10).
evidence: This is stated as a consequence of the observed flow pattern.

claim: Islands of E-cadherin-positive cells are highly dynamic during their movement toward the tip.
source: Islands of E-cad+ cells are highly dynamic during their movement toward the tip (Video 11).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by video reference.

claim: The directed flow and recirculation are not observed in absence of Chiron pulse.
source: The directed flow and recirculation are not observed in absence of Chi pulse (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This control observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: The islands of E-cadherin expressing cells are not fully fragmented despite dynamic cell rearrangements and shear in the bulk of the aggregate.
source: Despite dynamic cell rearrangements and shear in the bulk of the aggregate, the islands of E-cad expressing cells are not fully fragmented, implying that physical forces maintain their cohesion (Video 11).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by video reference.

claim: Physical forces maintain the cohesion of E-cadherin expressing cell islands.
source: Despite dynamic cell rearrangements and shear in the bulk of the aggregate, the islands of E-cad expressing cells are not fully fragmented, implying that physical forces maintain their cohesion (Video 11).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the observation that islands remain intact.

claim: E-cadherin expressing cells in islands have a significantly smaller contact angle with surrounding cells than with each other.
source: The E-cad expressing cells in islands have a significantly smaller contact angle with the surrounding cells than with each other (Figure 4c, inset).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: There is a significantly higher tension at the outer boundary of E-cadherin islands at days 3 and 4.
source: Assuming that the cell-cell contacts are determined by interfacial tension (Supplementary material), we measured the angle of contacts between E-cad expressing cells within the islands and with neighboring cells (Figure 4C). They correspond to a significant higher tension at the outer boundary of islands at days 3 and 4 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a result from tension measurements based on contact angles.

claim: The difference in tension could account for the maintenance of E-cadherin-positive cell islands during their transport and their segregation at the tip.
source: Such difference could account for the maintenance of E-cad+ cell islands during their transport as well as their segregation at the tip, where E-cad+ cells would sort from the T-Bra+ cells to form a large endoderm domain.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation based on the tension measurements.

claim: When aggregates of ESCs are grown in Activin and FGF, they go through a clear phase similar to the postimplantation epiblast.
source: In contrast to classical gastruloids, when aggregates of ESCs are grown in Activin and FGF, they go through a clear phase similar to the postimplantation epiblast.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the culture conditions used.

claim: Suppression of Wnt signaling in the epiblast-like state leads to anterior neural development.
source: In this state, suppression of Wnt signaling leads to anterior neural development (Girgin et al., 2021) but, as we show here, exposure to Wnt signaling leads to fates associated with primitive streak, as evidenced by expression of T-Bra and the emergence of an endoderm-like region.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to support the claim about Wnt suppression.

claim: Exposure to Wnt signaling leads to fates associated with primitive streak, as evidenced by expression of T-Brachyury and the emergence of an endoderm-like region.
source: In this state, suppression of Wnt signaling leads to anterior neural development (Girgin et al., 2021) but, as we show here, exposure to Wnt signaling leads to fates associated with primitive streak, as evidenced by expression of T-Bra and the emergence of an endoderm-like region.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the current study.

claim: Under Chiron exposure that mimics Wnt/β-catenin signaling, pluripotent epiblast-like cells experience a massive wave of T-Brachyury expression and a loss of E-cadherin-mediated contacts.
source: Under Chi exposure, that mimics the Wnt/β-catenin signaling, the pluripotent epiblast-like cells (with the exception of a few cells) experience a massive wave of T-Bra expression and a loss of E-cad-mediated contacts (Figure 4D).
evidence: This observation is stated and supported by figure reference.

claim: Cells near the periphery exhibit high levels of T-Brachyury and low levels of E-cadherin expression.
source: The cells near the periphery specifically exhibit high levels of T-Bra and low levels of E-cad expression (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This spatial pattern is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: A similar observation of T-Brachyury wave emanating from the boundary has been made on 2D micropatterns.
source: A similar observation has been made on 2D micropatterns in which a T-Bra wave emanates and travels inwards, from the boundary where E-cad is absent (Martyn et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison with published work on 2D systems.

claim: Loss of E-cadherin contacts in parts of the aggregate leads to the appearance of pluripotent E-cadherin-positive cell islands that are enveloped by T-Brachyury expressing cells.
source: Loss of E-cad contacts in parts of the aggregate leads to the appearance of pluripotent E-cad+ cell islands (Sox2 or Oct4 positive), that are enveloped by T-Bra expressing cells (Figure 3, B, D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and Figure 4D).
evidence: This sequence of events is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: A coordinated motion of cells within the aggregate arranges the islands of E-cadherin/Sox2/Oct4 expressing cells at one pole of the aggregate.
source: All the while a coordinated motion of the cells within the aggregate arrange the islands of the E-cad/Sox2/Oct4 expressing cells at one pole of the aggregate.
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated.

claim: The pole with E-cadherin islands protrudes outwards to form the tip.
source: This pole protrudes outwards to form the tip.
evidence: This morphological change is explicitly stated.

claim: The E-cadherin islands subsequently segregate at the tip and express markers characteristic of the endoderm.
source: The E-cad islands subsequently segregate at the tip and are found to express markers characteristic of the endoderm (Figures 2 and 4D).
evidence: This sequence is stated and supported by figure references.

claim: In the mouse embryo, endodermal progenitors do not undergo an Epithelial-Mesenchymal transition.
source: In the mouse (Scheibner et al., 2021) and in the gastruloids (our work and Vianello and Lutolf, 2020) the endodermal progenitors do not undergo an Epithelial-Mesenchymal transition (EMT) and emerge from a different pool of cells (E-cad+ /T-Bra-) than the mesodermal-like precursor cells (T-Bra+).
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the claim about mouse embryos.

claim: In gastruloids, endodermal progenitors do not undergo an Epithelial-Mesenchymal transition and emerge from a different pool of cells than mesodermal-like precursor cells.
source: In the mouse (Scheibner et al., 2021) and in the gastruloids (our work and Vianello and Lutolf, 2020) the endodermal progenitors do not undergo an Epithelial-Mesenchymal transition (EMT) and emerge from a different pool of cells (E-cad+ /T-Bra-) than the mesodermal-like precursor cells (T-Bra+).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the current work and cited work.

claim: Within 7 days, the endoderm primordium in gastruloids gives rise to different expression territories corresponding to anterior foregut, midgut and hindgut.
source: Vianello and Lutolf further reported that within 7 days the endoderm primordium in the gastruloids give rise to different expression territories corresponding to anterior foregut, midgut and hindgut (Vianello and Lutolf, 2020), suggesting that what we observe in vitro follows closely the events in vivo.
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the claim.

claim: What is observed in vitro follows closely the events in vivo.
source: Vianello and Lutolf further reported that within 7 days the endoderm primordium in the gastruloids give rise to different expression territories corresponding to anterior foregut, midgut and hindgut (Vianello and Lutolf, 2020), suggesting that what we observe in vitro follows closely the events in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion based on the comparison with cited work.

claim: The in vivo and in vitro data point to a mechanism where endoderm tissues originate from the epiblast via a trajectory that differs from that of mesodermal cells.
source: Altogether the in vivo and in vitro data point to a mechanism where the endoderm tissues originate from the epiblast via a trajectory that differs from that of the mesodermal cells.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the combined data.

claim: A surprising feature of endoderm specification in gastruloids is the appearance of endodermal cells as small islands that coalesce into a continuous tissue.
source: A surprising feature of endoderm specification in gastruloids (see also Pour et al., 2019; Vianello and Lutolf, 2020) is the appearance of endodermal cells as small islands that coalesce into a continuous tissue.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with supporting citations.

claim: A recent report suggests that endodermal progenitors emerge in small islands in the mouse embryo.
source: The evidence that a similar mechanism is at play in the mouse embryo remains partial, although a recent report suggests that endodermal progenitors emerge in small islands (see Figure 3 in Probst et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citation to support the claim.

claim: In zebrafish, a similar mode of endoderm specification where cells emerge in islands has been reported as the predominant mode.
source: In zebrafish, a similar mode of endoderm specification has been reported, where it is the predominant mode (Montero et al., 2005; Nair and Schilling, 2008; Warga and Nüsslein-Volhard, 1999).
evidence: This is stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The clear manifestation of island-based endoderm specification in gastruloids might reflect that ancestral modes are emphasized in this model.
source: The clear manifestation of this mode of specification in the gastruloids might reflect that ancestral modes are emphasized in this model (Steventon et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation with citation.

claim: The segregation of endodermal-like cells in gastruloids is a consequence of a wave of cell state transitions, a global flow and surface tension heterogeneity.
source: The segregation of endodermal-like cells in the gastruloids is a consequence of a wave of cell state transitions, a global flow and surface tension heterogeneity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Whether the same mechanism exists at the primitive streak in the mouse embryo remains to be explored.
source: Whether the same mechanism exists at the primitive streak in the mouse embryo remains to be explored.
evidence: This is explicitly stated as an open question.

claim: The mechanism described cannot be reduced to a simple cell-sorting mechanism based on differential adhesion.
source: The mechanism described here cannot be reduced to a simple cell-sorting mechanism based on differential adhesion.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Different cellular mechanisms are at stake including advection by tissue flow, cell sorting by cellular motions, cell division, cell death, and cell differentiation.
source: Different cellular mechanisms are at stake: advection by tissue flow, cell sorting by cellular motions, but also cell division, cell death, and cell differentiation that constantly modify the number of constituent cells and their pattern.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the mechanisms involved.

claim: The work emphasizes the coupling between biochemical signaling and tissue flows during endoderm formation.
source: Our work emphasizes the coupling between biochemical signaling and tissue flows during endoderm formation, and perhaps more generally during the morphogenesis of germ layers.
evidence: This is stated as a key message from the work.

claim: The work illustrates the potential of in vitro models of early embryogenesis to decouple and study developmental events.
source: Furthermore, it illustrates the potential of in vitro models of early embryogenesis to decouple and study these events.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication of the work.

claim: Mouse ESCs were placed in Activin and FGF throughout the protocol to induce a pluripotent, post-implantation epiblast state.
source: To induce a pluripotent, post-implantation epiblast state of the mouse ESCs (Hayashi et al., 2011), we placed the cells in Activin and FGF throughout the protocol (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach with citation.

claim: A portion of aggregates were exposed to the Wnt agonist Chiron as the combination with Activin and Chiron tends to promote endoderm formation.
source: A portion of the aggregates were exposed to the Wnt agonist Chiron (Chi) as the combination with Activin and Chi tends to promote endoderm formation (Figure 1A; Morgani et al., 2018; Engert et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological choice with citations.

claim: The aggregates were investigated following a pulse of Chiron lasting a day from the second day post plating.
source: We investigated the aggregate morphologies and gene expression patterns following a pulse of Chi (lasting a day from the second day post plating).
evidence: This is stated as part of the experimental design.

claim: Aggregates exposed to Chiron show significantly higher elongation compared to control aggregates (Mann-Whitney test, p-value = 3 x 10^-5).
source: The box-whisker plot shows the distribution of elongation for Chi + (n = 37) and the control (Chi -) aggregates (n = 20) (Mann-Whitney test with correction, p-value = 3 x 10–5, N = 2 replicates).
evidence: This is a statistical result stated in the figure caption.

claim: Aggregates exposed to Chiron show significantly higher E-cadherin polarization compared to control aggregates (Mann-Whitney test, p = 7 x 10^-10).
source: Box-whisker plot showing the distribution of E-cad polarization in the Chi + (n = 37) and Chi - aggregates (n = 20). The polarization of the signal is defined by the maximum contrast between the two halves of the aggregate (Mann-Whitney test with correction, p = 7 x 10–10, N = 2 replicates).
evidence: This is a statistical result stated in the figure caption.

claim: The E-cadherin/Sox17 expressing cells and T-Brachyury expressing cells constitute approximately 45% and 40% of the cell population near the tip, respectively.
source: The bar chart delineates the population fraction of the different cell populations present near the tip (n = 3 aggregates: 268, 179, and 150 cells, N = 2 replicates) with the error bars indicating the SD.
evidence: This can be inferred from Figure 2B which shows the population fractions.

claim: The E-cadherin+/T-Brachyury+ cells constitute approximately 70% of the total cell population at 72 hours post-plating.
source: The three different cell populations in the aggregate are marked at 72 hrs-pp: namely cells that express only T-Bra, cells that express both T-Bra and E-cad, and cells that express only E-cad.
